A little more about me

A few paths.
A clearer direction.

I’ve tried product, finance, and consulting. The work I keep coming back to puts me close to users and engineers, with enough ownership to build, measure, and improve.

The short story

Computer science
Financial curiosity
Product ownership

I studied Computer Science with a minor in Finance at BITS Pilani, Hyderabad Campus. I was drawn to ambiguous business problems and the ways technology could help solve them. Working with early-stage startups through the consulting group gave me an early view of product design, go-to-market decisions, and customer needs.

At JPMorgan, I worked on an internal platform for wholesale credit-risk analysis. Financial models, automation, migrations, and conversations with credit officers taught me why accuracy and trust matter so much in financial systems. I pursued the CFA and FRM exams to build deeper domain knowledge alongside the product work.

MoveInSync gave me the ownership I was looking for. As an early member of a new manufacturing-focused business unit, I worked across product, analytics, and customer operations—sometimes writing the requirements, sometimes building the first rough tool, and often working through the issue directly with a customer.

I explored consulting at Kearney to broaden that perspective. It taught me structured problem-solving and how to communicate technical trade-offs to senior stakeholders. It also clarified what I want next: long-term ownership, close collaboration with users and engineers, and the chance to keep improving what I ship.

“I like sitting close to the problem.”From my LinkedIn introduction

Building with other people

Good work
can make room for others.

As Vice President of BITS Hyderabad Consulting Group, I launched ProdEezy on one campus and scaled it to three, connecting 300+ students with 20+ product mentors. I also co-authored the first BITS consulting casebook.

As Secretary of the Wall Street Club, I led a 90-member finance community and launched its first newsletter, Upside. I was part of BlockSoc’s founding team, and supported 650+ students as a teaching assistant in Economics and Derivatives.
